articles.title: ‘Not really the thing to take a victory lap in’: the meaning of Jensen Huang’s new jacket
articles.summary: Nvidia’s boss has returned in a new uniform. But what does swapping leather for cotton say about power and leadership? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here. It’s been a big week for the stock market and the leather jacket-wearing community.
body: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, who had resigned as chief executive of the chipmaker after reports of multiple affairs, was reinstated as CEO. But as he returned to the company’s Silicon Valley headquarters surrounded by clapping employees chanting his name, one thing was amiss. Jensen was back, but the black leather jacket that had been his trademark piece for nearly two decades remained absent from its former power position. In its place? A navy cotton jacket.

In his first post-return company all-hands meeting, Huang apologised to employees, telling them he had made some “terrible mistakes”. He also said: “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around … I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”

What better than a humble cotton jacket to emphasise Huang’s newfound morality? A leather jacket comes with in-built bravado. It walks a fine line between confident and cocky, whereas its cotton cousin is much more subtle. It suggests modesty and restraint.
“I changed my jacket. I’m different now,” read one comment below a photo of a leather-less Huang. “Someone in fashion needs to make ‘The Jensen’ jacket right now,” read another.

articles.title: Mammy Goose is well and truly cooked in Glasgow’s incredibly random Aladdin
articles.summary: King’s theatre, Glasgow The offensive stereotypes have been ditched but this glitzy panto starring Elaine C Smith shoehorns in plenty of irrelevant material. Staging a traditional Aladdin in 2026 is problematic.
body: Stereotypes aside, Aladdin can still be a gripping coming-of-age story about greed and gullibility, poverty and power. The stakes can be loaded with deceit, jeopardy and cunning. In this version, set in the land of Pantomania, almost none of that survives.

Here, Widow Twankey has morphed into Mammy Goose (Elaine C Smith), inexplicably the proprietor of an ailing theatre. This is located near a haunted castle which, just as inexplicably, contains a panto hall of fame. Nice to see the portraits of previous King’s stars on display, but it is as irrelevant to the plot as the ballet moves of Priscilla the Goose (Oliver Moriarty), who is shoehorned into the action like so much else.

Just as extraneous are a tedious set-piece sketch involving the names of television programmes and a standard-issue haunted bedroom routine, complete with scripted ad-libs. With so much irrelevant material, the cave and the magic lamp seem like afterthoughts. So too does the featureless romance between Aladdin (Johnny Mac) and Princess Jemima (Blythe Jandoo), who scarcely get a chance to speak – let alone fall in love.
points: King’s theatre, Glasgow The offensive stereotypes have been ditched but this glitzy panto starring Elaine C Smith shoehorns in plenty of irrelevant material.

articles.title: Politician hosts 400,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state
articles.summary: Six helipads built and feast prepared by 500 cooks for wedding hosted by Anant Singh, an MP charged with murder. It takes a brave soul to try to match the mythic opulence of the wedding arranged by the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani for his son Anant in 2024.
body: Smaller fry though he is, Anant Singh, a legislator in India’s poorest state, Bihar, gave it his best shot on Wednesday, albeit in a rustic rural setting, for the nuptials of his daughter Shivangi Singh, and Rishikesh Kumar, an MBA student from Georgia State University in Atlanta.

About 400,000 guests were hosted across 2.5 hectares at the family home in the village of Nadawa – a staggering figure even by the standards of India’s famed extravagant weddings. Guests were treated to 500,000 pieces of traditional sweets, and a feast prepared by an army of 500 chefs and cooks, Singh’s confidant Munna Singh told Agence France-Presse. One thousand kgs of mutton were reportedly used for kebabs and curries. Six makeshift helipads were erected for VIPs flying in from across India.
Kumar arrived at the venue in sunglasses and waving an orange scarf in a convoy of 151 cars (Hindus consider uneven numbers to be lucky). Among the gifts for the groom was a Land Rover Defender.

The roads leading to the venue were so choked with cars before the wedding that one guest escaped the gridlock, The Times of India reported, by jumping on a tractor and driving across the surrounding fields.

articles.title: Zara’s Black Friday Sale Is Here—And the Best Finds Won’t Stay in Stock for Long
articles.summary: From essential knits to oversized outerwear and cold-weather accessories, shop the best-of-the-best of Zara’s Black Friday sale.
body: In a fashion landscape where retailers seem to offer discounts every other week, a Zara sale is a rare occurrence. The popular Spanish giant is notoriously selective about its markdowns, making its annual Black Friday event one of the most anticipated shopping opportunities of the year. Well, the wait is finally over: Zara’s Black Friday sale has arrived, bringing with it some of the best clothing deals of the season.

This year, as usual, the brand kicked things off early on its app, giving savvy shoppers a head start before the discounts hit the website and stores. With up to 40% off select styles, from clothing to footwear and handbags, there's plenty worth adding to your cart. But don’t wait too long: The best Zara Black Friday finds—and most popular sizes—rarely stick around. In particular, that’s true of Zara's luxe-looking outerwear, fashion-forward tailoring, and accessories that could easily pass for designer splurges.

articles.title: How Costume Designer Trish Summerville Reimagined ’70s Hollywood Style for ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’
articles.summary: From custom-printing vintage shirts for Brad Pitt to channeling Lauren Hutton for Elizabeth Debicki, the longtime David Fincher collaborator breaks down the film’s lived-in ’70s wardrobe.
body: Quentin Tarantino ’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood is rich in striking, darkly memorable imagery: Margot Robbie shimmying in a sunshine-yellow two-piece at the Playboy Mansion; the sunbaked menace of Brad Pitt’s visit to the Manson ranch; the audaciously bloody denouement, all pit bulls and flamethrowers, playing out high in the Hollywood Hills, with the glittering carpet of nighttime Los Angeles extending endlessly beyond.

But for some—this writer included—the film’s most indelible legacy is its costumes. And, more specifically, those of Pitt’s laid-back (and possibly wife-murdering) stuntman Cliff Booth. Double-denim layers, gold-rimmed aviators, scuffed moccasins—and, of course, those Hawaiian shirts—the character’s late-’60s California cool burnt up the screen and almost certainly played a part in the Americana wave that plenty of menswear fanatics are still riding.

Amazon has dropped the price of the two-pack Netgear Orbi 770 Series Wi-Fi 7 Mesh System to $449.99 from $549.99, saving you $100 on a setup that includes a router and a…
body: The system uses tri-band Wi-Fi 7 technology to spread your connection across three bands, with combined speeds of up to 11,000Mbps. It also supports wider 320MHz channels, though you'll need compatible Wi-Fi 7 devices to take advantage of those faster connections. If you prefer wired connections for devices that need a more stable link, the main router has three 2.5GbE LAN ports and a 2.5GbE WAN port, while the satellite offers two 2.5GbE LAN ports. This gives you plenty of room to connect a gaming console, desktop PC, or smart TV, and you can also use wired backhaul if your home has Ethernet cabling.

Once everything is connected, you can handle setup and day-to-day management through Netgear's Orbi app, while a web dashboard offers additional settings (for anyone who wants more control over their network), including VPN access and port forwarding, notes this PCMag review. There's no USB connectivity or 10GbE support, and some of its more advanced security and parental control features require a separate subscription after a free 30-day trial. Its Smart Parental Controls, for instance, cost $7.99 per month or $69.99 annually.

articles.title: The Body and The Teen Drama Fashion Machine
articles.summary: Coming-of-age series continue to flood streaming services. For fashion brands and resale platforms, they’re no longer a marketing pillar, but a fully fledged positioning strategy.
body: The Body, Overcompensating, Off Campus … Just when you thought pop culture had reached peak teen drama, the streaming giants release another slew of bingeable shows to capture the hearts of Gen Z and Gen Alpha viewers, and new audiences for their sponsors.

Taking the lion’s share of views at the moment is The Body, a coming-of-age psychodrama set in a Catholic school, which has quickly made its way into fashion fans’ For You pages. Just this week, the Netflix show has amassed 9.5 million views, marking its second week in the platform’s global top 10. It’s also currently the number one show in 39 countries.

Costumed by Mirren Gordon-Crozier, the series features iconic ‘00s designs, including the Dior Saddle bag, a Louis Vuitton x Takashi Murakami Pochette, a John Galliano-era “J’adore Dior” T-shirt, and various Juicy Couture accessories.
points: For fashion brands and resale platforms, they’re no longer a marketing pillar, but a fully fledged positioning strategy.

articles.title: The Art of Being Veruschka: Fashion Pays Tribute to a Legend
articles.summary: Generations of fashion’s image-makers, designers, and models reflect on the late Veruschka: the woman who made modeling an art form of its own.
body: “There is and will always be only one Veruschka,” Richard Avedon wrote in the May 1972 issue of Vogue in an impassioned tribute to his muse. More than half a century later, his words still ring true. Since news broke of the German supermodel’s death at the age of 87, generations of fashion’s image-makers, designers, and models have been reflecting on her immeasurable influence.

A protagonist of some of the most fantastical fashion editorials ever committed to the pages of Vogue and a prolific cover star, Veruschka helped expand the possibilities of what a model could be. Her body was her artistic medium, her imagination as instrumental to the making of a photograph as that of the person behind the lens. Her creative curiosity would endure long after her heyday in the 1960s and ’70s, finding expression in her experiments with body painting and camouflage, her performance art, and her occasional, much-feted returns to the runway.
points: Generations of fashion’s image-makers, designers, and models reflect on the late Veruschka: the woman who made modeling an art form of its own.

articles.title: The Oura Ring 5 Is $100 Off During Black Friday Sales
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Deal pricing and availability subject to change after time of publication. The Oura Ring 5 is the world’s smallest smart ring and looks more like a piece of stylish jewelry than a fitness tracker.
body: In addition to being 40% smaller than its predecessor, the Oura Ring 5 also lasts up to nine days longer than the Oura Ring 4, and has upgraded sensors for better accuracy. It’s completely waterproof and more durable, with increased scratch resistance, but still has the same discreet aesthetic, with a titanium build. It earned an Editors’ Choice Award from PCMag and has new features like long-term breathing-pattern measurements and overnight blood-pressure checks, joining the suite of features that track sleep, health, and activity trends.

It does charge an annual membership fee to access most of those features, so those looking for a basic fitness tracker might want to opt for a cheaper alternative like the Fitbit Air. However, if you’re shopping for a more robust screen-less health and fitness tracker with an exceptional, elegant design that feels lightweight and looks natural, the Oura Ring 5 is a worthwhile option.

articles.title: These Signature Sony Headphones Are Under $200 During Black Friday
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Deal pricing and availability subject to change after time of publication. The Sony WH-1000XM6 headphones are the most recent entry in Sony's 1000X series, which has been around since 2016.
body: The WH-1000XM5 are a generation older and were at the top of their class until they were supplanted by the XM6. On the plus side, by virtue of being older, they're currently discounted to $198 (down from the original $399.99) during Amazon's early Black Friday sale. That 50% off brings it down to the lowest price they've ever reached, a good deal for premium headphones that still sound incredible, even in 2026.

I have been a loyal customer of the 1000X line for many years; they're my go-to headphones for most activities. The WH-1000XM5 received an "outstanding" review from PCMag for their top-notch audio quality and exceptional audio when using the best-in-class active noise cancellation. The headphones are also well-designed to be comfortable for long listening sessions. The ear controls use tapping and swiping, which isn't my favorite, but it's what all modern headphones are moving toward. There's a companion app that lets you adjust your EQ settings to your liking, including what the swiping and tapping functions do.
